verses.2: Today, too, my complaint is bitter, the hand of my complaint is heavy on my affliction.
verses.3: Oh that I knew where I might find Him, that I might come even to His dwelling place!
verses.4: I would set my case before Him and fill my mouth with arguments.
verses.5: I would learn what He would answer me, and understand what He would say to me.
verses.6: Would a mighty one contend with me? No, only He would set it upon me.
verses.7: There is the just cause to be with Him, and I will escape forever from my judge.
verses.8: I went ahead, but He was not there; I looked behind, but I could not find Him.
verses.9: On His left He made me, but I did not grasp it; He wrapped His right hand, and I did not see.
verses.10: For He knows the way of mine, He has tested me as silver.
verses.11: My foot has held fast to His path; His way I have kept and did not lag.
verses.12: I did not turn away from His commands, but I kept His words within me.
verses.13: And He alone, who can oppose Him? What He desires, He does.
verses.14: For He fulfills His decree with many who are with Him.
verses.15: Therefore, before Him I am in awe, I consider and tremble because of Him.
verses.16: The God who has made my heart soft, and the Almighty has stirred me.
verses.17: For I was not concealed from darkness, and from my face He covered the gloom.

notes:
Notes
- v. 12: "I did not turn away from His commands" — "commands" renders מִצְוָה, which can also be "instruction" or "commandment."
- v. 13: "He alone, who can oppose Him?" — The Hebrew implies a rhetorical challenge to the idea of resisting God's will.
- v. 17: "I was not concealed from darkness" — The Hebrew is metaphorical, indicating that Job feels hidden or obscured by the divine.
